newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN agency probing $6 million housing scandal.
newsitem.headline: UN agency probing $6 million housing scandal.

text.p: Sixteen current and former U.N. staff are under investigation as a result of an audit that revealed $6 million in overpayments for construction costs in nine countries, a U.N. official said on Friday.

James Gustave Speth, administrator of the U.N. Development Programme, told a news conference two staff members had already been suspended and UNDP had stopped building staff housing and offices for itself and other U.N. agencies.
The $6 million, he said, accounted for 13 percent of the cost of the construction projects. UNDP operates in 150 countries and spends about $2 billion a year, mainly in the least developed countries.

Speth, an American who took over the four-year post in mid-1993, gave few details on the scandal and would not reveal identities or positions of the staff members involved or give many details of the suspected abuse.

"Swift and approriate corrective action will be taken," Speth said. "Sanctions will be applied to staff members wherever warranted. These could range from dismissal to reprimand as well as recovery of funds."
"I will do everything in my power to ensure that something like this never happens again," he said.

Speth said the construction work was done in the Maldives islands in the Indian Ocean and eight African countries: Zambia, Uganda, Ghana, Mozambique, Comoros, Sao Tome and Principe, Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde.
But he said the governments of these countries were not involved in the scandal.

Speth said the investigation covered an eight-year period. Asked why it took so long to discover the financial abuse, he said that plans on the drawing board did not come to fruition in recent years when the money was spent.
